resolution.summary: Change the consumer's override and base call from on_init(const hardware_interface::HardwareInfo & info) / SystemInterface::on_init(info) to on_init(const hardware_interface::HardwareComponentInterfaceParams & params) / SystemInterface::on_init(params) (PR #908, merge f59b61cd).
resolution.evidence: Maintainer: "Fixed with #908" (https://github.com/ros-controls/ros2_control_demos/issues/865). PR #908's CI on head aaa69032 passed (build (rolling), binary (rolling, main), semi_binary (rolling) and others, all 'success' on 2025-09-23), i.e. the fix was shown building against the ros2_control available to CI in September 2025, not against the broken provider revision 39c588eb; no source shows this exact resolved composition built.

notes: Class choice: the provider did not remove or change the old overload's parameter types; commit abbf8d63 added [[deprecated("Use on_init(const HardwareComponentInterfaceParams & params) instead.")]] to it and the new overload had been added by 8c520106 (#2323, 2025-06-25). The declaration changed while the element is still present, so element_retyped is used; the effect is a build warning only. consumer_built_against.broken = 7f92700b, the parent of abbf8d63 on master (2025-07-01), the last provider revision whose on_init(const HardwareInfo&) the consumer's source matches without the deprecation; inferred from the consumer's references, not stated in the source. consumer_built_against.resolved = the running provider 39c588eb, inferred because the fixed consumer's references (HardwareComponentInterfaceParams, on_init(params)) match its declarations; PR #908 itself was written in September 2025 against a later master. The issue says the same warning appears in all hardware components of the repository; PR #908 changed example_1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 14 and 16 as well, which are other compositions of the same kind and not conditions of this case. Later, ros2_control 8c6e2e9b ('Cleanup deprecations (#2589)', 2025-10-15) removed the on_init(const HardwareInfo&) overload, so the broken consumer would stop compiling against provider revisions from that point (element_removed_or_renamed, a failure); this is outside the reported composition. The issue references 'ros-controls/ros2_control/issues/2344', which is the PR merged as abbf8d63.
